theory.title: Closed Timelike Curves Make Quantum and Classical Computing Equivalent
theory.use: Motivation for distinguishing an ideal fixed-point resource from ordinary simulation; this script does not implement the paper's full PSPACE construction.

existing_repository.use: Transfer of the idea of explicitly checking a proposed fixed-point construction and its scope. No source code, Gaussian/Fock dynamics, or physics is imported.

map_definition: T_F(x)=x when F(x)=true; otherwise T_F(x)=(x+1) mod 2**n.
compact_map_cost: One CNF evaluation plus an n-bit increment; polynomial in the encoded formula and assignment lengths. Python integers and random bit access are not treated as unit-cost unbounded arithmetic.
important_distinctions: A single-state fixed point and a stationary probability distribution are different objects.
Compact map description and one map evaluation do not enumerate the exponentially many states.
This program explicitly enumerates all transitions to verify each finite instance, so it pays exponential time and memory.
The unsatisfiable walk cycles forever from a point state. An invariant uniform distribution exists without the walk converging to it.
The three chosen formula families are easy. The unique-family 2**n-1 walk proves no lower bound for SAT or for other algorithms.
Ideal fixed-point selection is an added computational resource. Neither physical CTCs nor a polynomial-time classical fixed-point solver are implemented.
This is a new finite classical experiment, not a direct insertion of SAT into the reference repository's Gaussian/Fock toy model.
Wall times are single-run diagnostics, not asymptotic evidence or controlled performance benchmarks.

checks: Mixed functional graph with two cycles, one absorber, and a transient
Hand-written two-bit truth tables for all three families
Every reported case additionally checks analytic family counts, cycle measures, and independent pruning

stationarity.check_method: Integer incoming counts verify uniform mass on every recurrent cycle; independent indegree pruning confirms the complete recurrent-node set.
stationarity.finite_graph_fact_used: Every stationary distribution of a finite deterministic transition system is a convex combination of uniform measures on its directed cycles; transient nodes have zero stationary mass.
stationarity.classification: Convex combinations of point masses at satisfying assignments.
stationarity.samples_only_note: The displayed examples are truncated; the counts and exact checks cover every recurrent class.

direct_compact_map_walk_from_zero.counting_convention: Steps exclude the final self-loop; the last map evaluation confirms absorption.

explicit_transition_table.memory_note: This is only the target array's packed n-bit lower-level representation size, not measured Python memory; Python objects and analysis arrays use more.
explicit_transition_table.scope: Exponential finite enumeration, separate from the compact formula and from one successor evaluation.
